Criteria:
- P1: Dependencies: does every step come after the steps whose results it needs? If a requirement of step B uses something that a requirement of step A creates (a name, a command, a connection, data, a schema, a part that is reused), B needs A. Name each missing dependency as 'A -> B' (A must finish before B) and say what B needs from A.
- P2: Coverage: is each requirement's work done by build and test steps that really do it?
- P3: Acceptance criteria: are they concrete and checkable?
- P4: Granularity: no duplicated steps and no step split into trivial pieces?

The research, verify, design and review steps and the order research -> design -> build -> test -> documents -> review come from a template and are correct. Steps listed as 'after: X' already depend on X (directly); a dependency through other steps also counts.

Material:
Requirements:
R1 [must] The server must accept at least 10 clients connected at the same time.
R2 [must] Each client must choose a unique nickname when it connects.
R3 [must] A message sent by one client must be delivered to every other connected client.
R4 [must] The server shall announce when a client joins or leaves the chat.
R5 [should] Clients should be able to send a private message with the command /msg.
R6 [could] The server may keep a history of the last 50 messages for new clients.
R7 [must] The server must not crash when a client disconnects without warning.
R8 [should] Messages should reach other clients within one second on a local network.

Plan steps:
research [research] Research the approach (requirements: -; after: -) criteria: every research question has an answer with sources; the answers name the options considered
verify [research] Check the research findings (requirements: -; after: research) criteria: every claim the design uses is supported by a source; unsupported claims are marked
design [design] Design the solution (requirements: -; after: verify) criteria: each part has a module and an interface; the skeleton runs; the design follows the constraints; C1 respected: Use Python 3.11 and the standard library only.
T1 [implement] Implement: The server must accept at least 10 clients conn… (+2) (requirements: R1, R2, R3; after: design) criteria: R1: The server must accept at least 10 clients connected at the same time.; R2: Each client must choose a unique nickname when it connects.; R3: A message sent by one client must be delivered to every other connected client.
T3 [implement] Implement: The server shall announce when a client joins o… (+2) (requirements: R4, R5, R6; after: T1) criteria: R4: The server shall announce when a client joins or leaves the chat.; R5: Clients should be able to send a private message with the command /msg.; R6: The server may keep a history of the last 50 messages for new clients.
T2 [test] Check: The server must accept at least 10 clients connec… (+2) (requirements: R1, R2, R3; after: T1) criteria: R1 works as stated; R2 works as stated; R3 works as stated
T4 [test] Check: The server shall announce when a client joins or… (+2) (requirements: R4, R5, R6; after: T3) criteria: R4 works as stated; R5 works as stated; R6 works as stated
T5 [test] Check quality of the work (requirements: R7, R8; after: T3) criteria: R7: The server must not crash when a client disconnects without warning.; R8: Messages should reach other clients within one second on a local network.
T6 [document] Prepare README (requirements: -; after: T2, T4, T5) criteria: D2 exists: README; it matches the finished, tested work
T7 [document] Prepare Design and test report (requirements: -; after: T2, T4, T5) criteria: D3 exists: Design and test report; it matches the finished, tested work
review [review] Final review (requirements: -; after: T6, T7) criteria: every must requirement is met; every deliverable is present; C1 respected: Use Python 3.11 and the standard library only.; C2 respected: Use TCP sockets; do not use a web framework.
